\chapter{Tharo Naam: Ask One Name}
\label{ch:mw-name-question}
\hlchaptermodality{6}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can ask \mw{थारो} \mw{नाम} \mw{कांई} \mw{है} and answer with a chosen name in four separately scored skills.}

The question half of the name exchange, built by ear before three new signs are isolated and joined to the already-secure answer.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[thāro]{Hear \emph{thāro} — turn from my to your}

\label{lesson:MW-C05-hear-tharo}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{mhāro nām rām hai} once. Write \textbf{\mw{न}}, then \textbf{\mw{है}}, from memory. Point to yourself on \emph{mhāro}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{thāro} — \textbf{your}, before a masculine singular noun
\end{quote}

Listen twice: \emph{thā-ro}. Let a small breath follow \emph{t}. Point to another person when you hear it. Spelling waits for the next lesson.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear \emph{mhāro} and point to yourself. Hear \emph{thāro} and point gently away. Change the order twice.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say the pair once: \emph{mhāro} — my; \emph{thāro} — your.

Sources: \href{https://nepal.sil.org/resources/archives/63768}{SIL International, \emph{Marwari–English Dictionary} (2015)} and \href{https://www.rgmcet.edu.in/assets/img/documents/Campus\%20Life/Other\%20Reports.pdf}{Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat language report}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[tha]{\mw{थ} — one breathed consonant}

\label{lesson:MW-W05-tha}



\begin{quote}
Read \textbf{\mw{हां}}, say \textbf{yes}, then hear \emph{thāro}, point away, and say \textbf{your}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script}
\begin{quote}
\mw{थ}
\end{quote}

Read \textbf{\mw{थ}} as \emph{tha}: the tongue begins near the teeth and a small breath follows. It is one new shape. The remaining signs in \emph{thāro} are already known.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Keep \textbf{\mw{थ}} visible. Finger-trace it once, then trace one printed model once. Say \emph{tha} after your hand stops.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Cover the model and write \textbf{\mw{थ}} once.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[thāro]{\mw{थारो} — your}

\label{lesson:MW-C05-tharo}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{thāro} and its meaning. Read \textbf{\mw{म्हारो}} and give the opposite direction: my.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{थ}} + \textbf{\mw{ा}} + \textbf{\mw{रो}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{थारो}} — \emph{thāro} — your
\end{quote}

Only \textbf{\mw{थ}} was new. The rest comes from \textbf{\mw{राम}} and \textbf{\mw{म्हारो}}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look for five seconds, cover \textbf{\mw{थारो}}, wait five seconds, then write it. Uncover and compare \textbf{\mw{थ}}, \textbf{\mw{ा}}, and \textbf{\mw{रो}} separately.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Read the two words once without romanization.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kāĩ]{Hear \emph{kāĩ} — what}

\label{lesson:MW-C05-hear-kain}



\begin{quote}
Retrieve \textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा}} once by ear, voice, eye, and writing; point to \textbf{\mw{ै}} in \textbf{\mw{है}}. Then read \textbf{\mw{थारो}}, hear \emph{thāro nām}, and give its meaning: \textbf{your name}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{kāĩ} — what
\end{quote}

Listen for one long, lightly nasal middle and a final long \emph{ī}. Say the whole word once rather than exaggerating the nasal sound. Its old interrogative root belongs to the same deep family as Sanskrit \emph{kim} and English \emph{what}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear \emph{thāro nām kāĩ hai?} Point to the question mark and say \textbf{What is your name?} No spelling yet.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say the four-beat question once from sound.

Sources: \href{https://nepal.sil.org/resources/archives/63768}{SIL International, \emph{Marwari–English Dictionary} (2015)}, \href{https://dsal.uchicago.edu/dictionaries/soas/}{Turner, \emph{A Comparative Dictionary of the Indo-Aryan Languages}}, and \href{https://rsad.artandculture.rajasthan.gov.in/content/dam/doitassets/art-and-culture/Rajasthani-Bhasha-Sahitya-Avm-Sanskriti-Academy-Bikaner/pdf/jjpdf/JJ\_28\_06\_06\_September\_to\_September\_1999.pdf}{Rajasthan Sahitya Akademi, \emph{Jāgtī Jot}, September 1999}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ka]{\mw{क} — the first sign in \emph{kāĩ}}

\label{lesson:MW-W05-ka}



\begin{quote}
Hear \emph{kāĩ} and say \textbf{what}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script}
\begin{quote}
\mw{क}
\end{quote}

Read \textbf{\mw{क}} as \emph{ka}. Keep the sound short and unaspirated. Only this one shape is new today.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Keep \textbf{\mw{क}} visible. Finger-trace it once, then trace one printed model once. Say \emph{ka} after your hand stops.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Cover the model and write \textbf{\mw{क}} once.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ī]{\mw{ई} — long \emph{ī} standing alone}

\label{lesson:MW-W05-ii-independent}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\mw{प}}, then \textbf{\mw{क}}, once each. Point to attached \textbf{\mw{ी}} in \textbf{\mw{पाणी}} and say its long vowel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script}
\begin{quote}
\mw{ई}
\end{quote}

Read \textbf{\mw{ई}} as long \emph{ī}. Use this independent form when the vowel stands on its own. Attached \textbf{\mw{ी}} still belongs after a consonant.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Keep \textbf{\mw{ई}} visible and copy it once. Then point: \textbf{\mw{ई}} stands alone; \textbf{\mw{ी}} attaches.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Cover the model, wait three seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{ई}} once.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kāĩ]{\mw{कांई} — what, with no new sign}

\label{lesson:MW-C05-kain}



\begin{quote}
Write known \textbf{\mw{ण}} and new \textbf{\mw{थ}} once each. Say \emph{kāĩ} and its meaning, then write \textbf{\mw{क}} and independent \textbf{\mw{ई}}. Point to the known nasal dot in \textbf{\mw{हां}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{क}} + \textbf{\mw{ा}} + \textbf{\mw{ं}} + \textbf{\mw{ई}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{कांई}} — \emph{kāĩ} — what
\end{quote}

No shape is new. Read the whole word smoothly; the dot lightly nasalizes the long middle rather than creating an extra beat.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look for five seconds, cover \textbf{\mw{कांई}}, wait five seconds, and write it. Uncover and compare \textbf{\mw{क}}, \textbf{\mw{ा}}, \textbf{\mw{ं}}, and \textbf{\mw{ई}} separately.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Read \textbf{\mw{थारो} \mw{नाम} \mw{कांई} \mw{है}?} once without romanization.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Practice — ask one name and give one name}

\label{lesson:MW-C05-practice}



\begin{quote}
Say the four older meanings as you hear \emph{rām-rām sā, ābhār, hā(n) sā,} and \emph{pāṇī}. Write only \textbf{\mw{पाणी}} from the last cue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{थारो} \mw{नाम} \mw{कांई} \mw{है}?}
\end{quote}

>

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{म्हारो} \mw{नाम} \mw{राम} \mw{है।}}
\end{quote}

The question asks \textbf{What is your name?} The answer says \textbf{My name is Ram.} In speech, replace \emph{rām} with the name the speaker chooses. This book teaches one documented central-Marwari form; regional speakers may use another possessive or copula, and that variation is not an error.

\subsection*{Your turn}
1. \textbf{Listen:} hear one of the two lines and identify question or answer. 2. \textbf{Speak:} hear the question and answer with a chosen name, without notes. 3. \textbf{Read:} match the printed question to the printed answer. 4. \textbf{Write:} hear the question, wait ten seconds, and write it with no model.

Score each line separately. Speaking cannot cover a missing word in writing; reading cannot cover an unanswered spoken question.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop after one complete exchange. Accuracy comes before speed.

Sources: \href{https://www.rgmcet.edu.in/assets/img/documents/Campus\%20Life/Other\%20Reports.pdf}{Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat language report}, \href{https://nepal.sil.org/resources/archives/63768}{SIL International, \emph{Marwari–English Dictionary} (2015)}, and \href{https://rsad.artandculture.rajasthan.gov.in/content/dam/doitassets/art-and-culture/Rajasthani-Bhasha-Sahitya-Avm-Sanskriti-Academy-Bikaner/pdf/jjpdf/JJ\_28\_06\_06\_September\_to\_September\_1999.pdf}{Rajasthan Sahitya Akademi, \emph{Jāgtī Jot}, September 1999}.
\end{tcolorbox}
